content:
I've noticed that I spend a lot of time repeatedly fixing the same style issues. Perhaps it's time we added a linter to the project? I made a PR adding the batteries linter, but our code has hundreds of errors (edit: over 7000!) by that standard at the moment, and I'm wanted to get you folks thoughts on what we should do:

  • Use the batteries linter, fix the errors
  • Write a custom lint driver for now with just the stuff that we find ourselves fixing
  • No linter or something else
Common things are like, including names for instances (I have been bad about this), starting lines with a colon or putting line breaks in the wrong places, long lines, non-terminal simps etc.
Some may be subject to upstreaming with all the ongoing changes to linters, but currently a few of these are syntax linters in Mathlib, right?
I think you're the expert here, but I'm new to this and still trying to figure out what is available where yeah. Tbh I wouldn't care so much if we had to copy/paste mathlib linters though

As an example, docs#Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.longLine for line length, docs#Mathlib.Linter.linter.flexible for non-terminal simp. I personally would be find having to replicate these unfortunate maintenance-wise, but it should be possible.

One thing I suggest from experience: for syntax linters in a project with minimal to no Mathlib dependency, you have to think a bit harder about making sure your linters are available in every file. In CSLib what we did was mirror Mathlib and have a Cslib/Init.lean that we check is imported in every file. If you just use weak.* in your lakefile, the problem is that you can silently have files in leaf modules that forget to import the linters.
Interesting. Is that just for linting while editing or will lake lint not catch files that don't import the linters?

This is for syntax linters, the ones that run while editing. lake lint is usually configured (for instance the batteries lint driver you mention) to run environment linters that require the "complete" environment from lake build.
(again there are a couple of new options to lake lint on the latest toolchains that I'm not sure about yet, but this is the current state of things in CSLib for instance)

Markus de Medeiros said:

starting lines with a colon

I admit I do this deliberately, because this way it's easier to see the statement of a theorem.

I think having more linters would be great! At the moment it feels like everyone writes code in a slightly different style and trying to get this to a uniform shape without linters is very tedious.

Chris Henson said:

In CSLib what we did was mirror Mathlib and have a Cslib/Init.lean that we check is imported in every file.

I think this would also be very useful for Iris Lean!
There's no hope of having a formatter instead of a linter, right? I'm not too familiar how developed these kinds of tools are for Lean
A formatter is on the way and will likely be deployed probably at some point later this year.
In the meantime, I'm wondering if there are any other ideas for linters we should try to write (or copy from mathlib?) Asking more for what the other Iris-Lean reviewers have encountered so far.

On the PR Sergei also suggested starting by ignoring every file, and then iteratively cleaning the repo. It's a good idea (especially if we have a nice tracker for it), and it also means we're free to choose more aggressive linting options upfront.

Having linters would be great and gradually fixing the files is a good idea.
We should add them asap so new files are linted. I think we could just use the batteries linter as a starting point, before having a complete list of rules.

The points you mentioned at the start are all good. Do you know which we can copy-paste from Mathlib and which we need to implement ourselves?

4.31 adds some linting btw!

Lake: Built-in Linting🔗

Lake gains a built-in linting framework, accessible through lake lint flags (#13393, #13431). It ships with environment linters upstreamed from Batteries/Mathlib (defLemma/defProp, checkUnivs) — see also the core upstreaming in #13356 — and a builtinLint package configuration option. Flags include --builtin-lint, --builtin-only, --clippy, --lint-all, and --lint-only <name>, and a @[builtin_nolint] attribute suppresses specific linters per declaration.

#13513 extends this to text linters by persisting their warnings into each module's .olean, and #13843 makes module-system targets lint their public surface, matching what downstream consumers see.
